title: Fixed-degree comparison of the Grothendieck edge and the cocycle quotient
statement: Let F: A -> B and G: B -> C be additive left exact functors between Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-composite-acyclicity], with derived categories, and assume F sends injectives to G-acyclics. Let X be an object of A, I an injective resolution of X [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and n a natural number. Put K=F(I) and T=(F composed with G)(I). Let c: G(Z^n(K)) -> Z^n(T) be any morphism satisfying c composed with iCycles_T = G(iCycles_K). Then c composed with the quotient Z^n(T) -> H^n(T), the inverse comparison H^n(T) -> R^n(F composed with G)(X), the canonical Grothendieck left edge [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps], and G of the comparison R^nF(X) -> H^n(K), equals G of the quotient Z^n(K) -> H^n(K). The comparisons are those of [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]; the right derived functors and degree-zero identifications are those of [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. This is a fixed-degree equation for a supplied c; it asserts neither existence of c, filtration properties nor collapse.

proof.text: Let K=F(I). Extend K by zero to integer degrees and choose a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution with its shared augmentation by [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists]. Package it in a CartanEilenbergPresentation with the given X and I. Apply [lem-pc-grothendieck-ss-double-complex-model] to obtain the total augmentation a, its cohomology comparison h and the quotient/inclusion description of the abstract left edge. The equation for homologyMap a identifies h with the inverse of I.isoRightDerivedObj (F composed with G).

proof.text: Every F(I^q) is G-acyclic by [def-sp-composite-acyclicity] and the injectivity in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Applying G to the CE augmentation in each resolved column is a quasi-isomorphism. The injective horizontal cycles, boundaries and cohomology of [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists] give split short exact sequences, so G commutes with horizontal cohomology. The second filtration has E2^{0,n}=G(H^n(K)) through rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf, and the model fixes its canonical identification with G(R^nF(X)).

proof.text: Precompose homologyMap a with c followed by the homology quotient of GF(I). The condition c composed with iCycles = G(iCycles) fixes its representative in the resolution-degree-zero total summand. The quotient by filtration step 1 discards positive resolution degrees. Under the split horizontal-cohomology computation, the degree-zero component is G applied to the quotient Z^n(K) -> H^n(K). The stable-page cycle inclusion into E2 preserves this component. Substitute the explicit augmentation and left-edge equations of [lem-pc-grothendieck-ss-double-complex-model], and compose the target with G of I.isoRightDerivedObj F n. This gives exactly the stated equation. The calculation applies to every c with the stated inclusion equation since iCycles is monic. More explicitly, if U is the horizontal row in resolution degree zero, a_Z: Z^n(K) -> Z^n(U) and b: H^n(K) -> H^n(U) are induced by the CE augmentation, then a_Z followed by the quotient of U equals the quotient of K followed by b, by homology-map naturality. Applying G and the split-horizontal-homology identification gives exactly the degree-zero representative of G(quotient_K) followed by G(b). The augmentation b lands in the kernel of the next resolution differential. The degree-zero comparison identifies this kernel with G(H^n(K)), and there is no incoming boundary from a negative resolution degree. The transpose sign is (-1)^(n*0)=1 on this representative.
